title: Ordinary module open comparisons respect the open counits
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq Y$ an arbitrary open, $V=h^{-1}U$, $g:V\to U$ the restricted morphism, and $j_X:V\to X$, $j_Y:U\to Y$ the inclusions. Let $L_X,L_Y$ be schemeOpenRestriction, $R_X,R_Y$ the module direct images along the inclusions, and $G=g_*$. Let $\beta:R_Xh_*\cong GR_Y$ and $\alpha:h_*L_Y\cong L_XG$ be the fixed UNDERIVED ordinary-module comparisons [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-open-counit-model], and let $\varepsilon_X,\varepsilon_Y$ be the ordinary open adjunction counits [def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data]. For every ordinary sheaf of modules $M$ on $V$, $L_Y(\beta_M);\varepsilon_{Y,GM}=\alpha_{R_XM};G(\varepsilon_{X,M})$. This is an equality of sheaf-module morphisms, with no complex or homotopy category in its statement.

source.place: Tag 08FE, proof: the underived open restriction/direct-image identity; Tag 08BV, open restriction maps. Official pages https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08FE and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08BV read 2026-10-14. The counit normalization calculation expands the existing parent proof.

proof.text: Transport from schemeOpenRestriction to restrictFunctor using overFunctorEquiv. The definition of schemeOpenModuleAdjunction is ofNatIsoLeft with the inverse of this equivalence, so its counit is overFunctorEquiv.hom followed by restrictAdjunction.counit. Naturality moves the Y equivalence past the comparison; the X inverse/hom cancel. It suffices to verify the resulting restrictFunctor square on sections.

For an open W of U, the composition comparison has section maps given by identity, restriction along the equality of inverse-image opens from morphismRestrict_ι, and identity. The Y counit uses the equality j_Y inverse image (j_Y image W) = W. The restriction comparison uses image_morphismRestrict_preimage to identify h inverse image (j_Y image W) with j_X image (g inverse image W); its pushforwardCongr₂ component is the presheaf restriction along this equality. Applying G to the X counit then restricts along j_X inverse image (j_X image (g inverse image W)) = g inverse image W. In both cases the resulting map on an element is M.presheaf.map of the equality arrow between the common source open and g inverse image W. Functoriality combines the restrictions and thinness identifies the arrows.
Apply the sectionwise component theorem on every open and then extensionality on section elements.
